description: We’re a multidisciplinary team excited about space, technology, creativity, and innovation. 🚀 We bring together skills in coding, design, research, and problem-solving to turn bold ideas into practical, engaging solutions. We’re ready to learn, collaborate, and bring our ideas to life!
summary: When astronauts are on space missions that can last from weeks to over a year, it’s common to face numerous hazards that can impact their physical state, like radiation and microgravity. Regular health monitoring is a must to help detect health risks early before they manifest into an illness. AstroVitals is a health monitoring system for astronauts and the crew medical officer on board the spacecraft to help them during space flights. The software captures data on various health parameters including heart rate, blood pressure, blood glucose, oxygen saturation, body temperature, sleep, mood, and symptoms. The application processes the available data to provide an indicative health score, health status levels and alerts. It suggests the necessary actions according to the detected problems including urgent notifications about the critical health condition.
details:
AstroVitals is a web-based health-monitoring prototype designed to support astronauts and onboard Crew Medical Officers in monitoring crew health during space missions. The platform focuses on seven key health indicators: heart rate, blood pressure, blood glucose, oxygen saturation, body temperature, sleep, and mood.

Unlike basic health-tracking systems, AstroVitals combines individual health readings, symptom assessments, and historical trends to help identify potential health concerns. It uses four alert levels to communicate the severity of health conditions and recommend appropriate actions, supporting early identification and informed decision-making in space environments.

How It Works

AstroVitals allows astronauts to record health measurements through guided, step-by-step instructions. Users can select health checks through an interactive body map or use the symptom checker to identify potential concerns.

The system evaluates recorded readings using four color-coded alert levels:

  • Normal
  • Needs Attention
  • Contact the Crew Medical Officer
  • Emergency

It also tracks historical health trends, identifies combinations of concerning readings, and generates editable medical reports for flight surgeons when further medical attention is required. The prototype supports different mission environments, including spacecraft, space stations, and lunar bases.

Key Benefits & Impact

  • Supports astronauts in monitoring and understanding their health status.
  • Helps identify potentially concerning health patterns through combined readings.
  • Provides recommended actions based on the severity of health alerts.
  • Facilitates communication between astronauts, onboard medical personnel, and ground-based medical teams.
  • Generates editable medical reports to support medical assessment and decision-making.
  • Offers a structured health-monitoring approach adaptable to different space mission environments.

Tools & Technologies

  • HTML: Structures the web application's content and interface.
  • CSS: Handles styling, layout, and visual presentation.
  • JavaScript: Implements interactive features, health assessments, alert levels, and application functionality.
  • Super Intelligence: Used as an AI-assisted development tool to support implementation, refine functionality, and improve the development process.

Creative Elements

  • Interactive body map for selecting specific health checks.
  • Step-by-step measurement instructions to guide astronauts.
  • Symptom checker for identifying potential health concerns.
  • Visual alert system with four levels of medical severity.
  • Historical health trends to support monitoring over time.
  • Editable medical reports for communicating health information.
  • Adaptable interface designed for different space mission environments.
